params.why: numerator zero must not coincide with a denominator zero

stem: Find the values of $x$ that must be excluded from the domain of the function $n(x)=\frac{x-{=p}}{x^2-{=k2}}$. Give both values.
solution: The domain is R minus the zeroes of the denominator, so solve $x^2-{=k2}=0$.
The domain is $R-\{{=k},-{=k}\}$, so the excluded values are ${=k}$ and $-{=k}$.

proposed_misconceptions.label: Finds only the positive root of the denominator
proposed_misconceptions.description: Gives only x = sqrt(k) and loses the negative root.

notes: Standard: x^2 - k^2 denominator, two excluded values. Numerator zero p avoided equal to k.
